entry.title: grapefruit (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the grapefruit (examples pictured) was described as the "forbidden fruit" in 1750?

entry.title: Ian Fyfe (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that British war correspondent Ian Fyfe was killed on D-Day while landing in a glider with troops attacking the Merville Gun Battery?

entry.title: Itim (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the 1976 Philippine film Itim was described as "one of the most remarkable debuts in cinema history" in a 2022 retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art?

entry.title: Phoebe Plummer (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Phoebe Plummer was "unfortunate" to draw Christopher Hehir as judge when they stood trial over the Just Stop Oil Sunflowers protest?

entry.title: Belvidere Apollo Theatre collapse (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the only death from the Belvidere Apollo Theatre collapse was the one audience member who bought a concert t-shirt from Crypta that night, according to their lead singer?

entry.title: Music from the Merch Desk (2016–2023) (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the cover art of Music from the Merch Desk (2016–2023) was derived from bootleg merchandise?

entry.title: Michael O'Kane (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Michael O'Kane never received approval to begin constructing a building for the College of the Holy Cross?

entry.title: Moturoa Island (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that in the 1980s, when Moturoa Island lost all its endangered kiwi to pests, experts reintroduced seven birds – today there could be as many as 300 kiwi on the island?

entry.title: Jill, Duchess of Hamilton (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Jill, Duchess of Hamilton, donated her body to science because "funerals are a bore"?
